title: Determination of thermodynamics from entanglement entropy in the finite-density O(N) model
authors: Niko Jokela, Aatu Rajala, Tobias Rindlisbacher
abstract: We nonperturbatively compute Rényi entropies for strip-shaped subregions in the three-dimensional O(4) model at finite density on the lattice. By using a dual variable representation and a tailored worm algorithm, we circumvent the sign problem when sampling the grand canonical ensemble. In the limit of large subregions, we also establish a direct, quantitative relationship between the derivative of entanglement entropy with respect to the size of the entangling region and the thermal entropy density for general quantum field theories, providing a new way to study their thermodynamics. We corroborate this argument with our lattice results by demonstrating that, in the appropriate limit, the derivative of entanglement entropy satisfies the same Maxwell relation as the thermal entropy density.
summary: The paper develops a method to calculate entanglement entropy in the finite-density O(4) model using advanced lattice techniques. It establishes a key theoretical result showing that the rate of change of entanglement entropy with respect to region size directly measures the system's thermal entropy density. This offers a novel, nonperturbative pathway to study thermodynamics using quantum information metrics.
main_problem: The central goal is to establish a quantitative, nonperturbative relationship between entanglement entropy (EE) and the thermal entropy density ($s$) in Quantum Field Theories (QFTs), especially at finite chemical potential.
main_result: The derivative of the entanglement entropy with respect to the size of the entangling region ($\partial 	ext{SEE}/\partial \ell$) is shown to directly yield the thermal entropy density ($s$) in the limit of large subregions, satisfying a generalized Maxwell relation.
method: The authors use lattice field theory techniques on the O(4) model, employing a dual variable representation and a tailored worm algorithm to compute Rényi entropies nonperturbatively while circumventing the sign problem at finite density.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the three-dimensional O(4) model simulated on a lattice at finite chemical potential ($\mu$). The analysis is generalizable to other interacting quantum field theories.
key_observables: Rényi entropies, Entanglement Entropy (SEE), Thermal entropy density ($s$), and the derivative of SEE with respect to subregion size ($\ell$).
important_parameters: Finite density regime (chemical potential $\mu$), large subregions limit ($\ell 	o \infty$), and the replica parameter $r 	o 1$.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes that in the appropriate thermodynamic limit, bulk properties are governed by free energy densities, allowing the derivative of EE to isolate thermal quantities.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes a general framework connecting EE derivatives to thermodynamic potentials using replica methods. It then applies these techniques nonperturbatively to the O(4) model on the lattice at finite density, culminating in the demonstration of the Maxwell relation equivalence.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool showing that fundamental thermodynamic quantities like entropy can be extracted purely from quantum information measures (entanglement), which is highly relevant for understanding many-body physics beyond standard thermal measurements.

Then the head ϕ+ is moved to a neighboring site x′ = x + bα and kx,α is shifted by ±1 to compensate. This is continued until the head and tail are again on the same site when they can be removed. Alternatively, if ϕ−had been chosen as the head, the process would be the same except the signs would be reversed.

Figure 4. A diagram of a disconnected worm move. By shift- ing px and px′ in the k-sector or n(i) x and n(i) x′ in the χi sector, the worm head can be removed and reinserted into any site on the lattice. The variable shifted at the new site x′ can also be of a different type than the one at x, which allows for changing the head type.
